'''Ronald Crosby Davidson''' (3 July 1941 – 19 May 2016) was a Canadian [[physicist]], professor, and scientific administrator who worked in the United States.  He served as the first director of the [[MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center]] from 1978 to 1988, and as director of the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]] from 1991 to 1996.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Ronald C. Davidson |magazine=The Scientist |date=7 January 1991 |url=http://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/11572/title/Ronald-C--Davidson/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Ronald C Davidson Professor of Astrophysical Sciences, Emeritus. Senior Astrophysicist|publisher=Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory|url=http://www.pppl.gov/people/ronald-c-davidson|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130105063452/http://www.pppl.gov/people/ronald-c-davidson|archivedate=2013-01-05}}</ref>  He had been Professor of Astrophysical Sciences at [[Princeton University]] since 1991.

Davidson was born in [[Norwich, Ontario]], Canada. He received his [[bachelor's degree]] from [[McMaster University]] in 1963 and his [[doctorate]] in physics from [[Princeton University]] in 1966. He was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1966 to 1968. In 1968, he went to teach at the [[University of Maryland]], where he became a full professor in 1972. In 1978, he moved to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he taught until 1991.

Davidson was a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. He received the Leadership Award from Fusion Power Associates in 1986 and the 2005 IEEE Particle Accelerator Science and Technology Award.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PPPL physicist Davidson Garners 2005 Particle Accelerator Science and Technology Award|date=3 May 2005|publisher=PsychCentral|url=http://psychcentral.com/news/archives/2005-05/dppl-ppd050305.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216234306/http://psychcentral.com/news/archives/2005-05/dppl-ppd050305.html|archivedate=16 December 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2008, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for "''pioneering contributions to the physics of one-component [[non-neutral plasmas]], intense charge [[Particle beam|particle beams]], and collective nonlinear interaction processes in high-temperature plasmas.''"<ref>{{Cite web|title=2008 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient |publisher=American Physical Society (APS) |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Davidson&first_nm=Ronald&year=2008 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516053104/http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Davidson&first_nm=Ronald&year=2008 |archivedate=16 May 2011 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Davidson was a resident of [[Cranbury, New Jersey]]. He died on May 19, 2016, at his home.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=2016-05-30 |title=Ronald C. Davidson, Pioneer of Fusion Power, Dies at 74 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/30/science/ronald-c-davidson-pioneer-of-fusion-power-dies-at-74.html |access-date=2026-05-29 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
